title: Pointwise Multipliers of Dyadic Besov Spaces via Haar-Fourier Coefficients
content: For a function \( \varphi \) on [0,1] let \( T_\varphi \) be the operator which maps the Haar--Fourier coefficients of f to the Haar-Fourier coefficients of the product \( f\varphi \). We study the class \( \mathcal{M}(b^{s}_{p,q}) \) of those \( \varphi \) for which \( T_\varphi \) is bounded on the dyadic Besov sequence space \( b^{s}_{p,q} \); by Triebel's theorem this is the class of pointwise multipliers of the Besov space \( B^{s}_{p,q}[0,1] \) in the range 1/p-1<s<1/p, and it contains the multipliers of \( \ell^{p} \) as the special case \( s=1/p-1/2 \). We prove that \( \mathcal{M}(b^{s}_{p,q})\subset L^{\infty} \) always, with strict inclusion unless s=0; that \( \mathcal{M}(b^{s}_{p,q})=\mathcal{M}(b^{-s}_{p',q'}) \) with equality of norms; and we give an exact formula for the multiplier norm on \( b^{s}_{1,1} \), 0<s<1, in terms of a Carleson-type condition on the dyadic oscillations of $\varphi$. Two independent sufficient conditions follow: \( \varphi\in B^{s}_{1/s,1} \) (sharp in the third index) and \( \varphi \) of bounded variation, the latter with explicit constants. Using Stein's interpolation theorem for analytic families we show that \( \mathcal{M}(b^{s}_{1,1})\subset\mathcal{M}(b^{\sigma}_{p,q}) \) whenever -s/p'<\( \sigma \)<s/p; consequently every function of bounded variation is a Haar multiplier of every $b^{\sigma}_{p,q}$ in Triebel's range -1/p'<\( \sigma \)<1/p, and \( \mathrm{BV}\cup B^{1/2}_{2,1}\subset\mathcal{M}(\ell^{1})\subset\mathcal{M}(\ell^{p})\subsetneq L^{\infty} \) for \( p\neq 2 \).
